summary.prose: Run two chats in the same repository independently, including when one waits for an approval. Switching back restores the running chat’s progress and elapsed time. The queue still preserves message order within each chat and keeps Stop and decisions scoped to that chat. This standalone design follows approved ISSUE-d8b2fe8e08f1d1be. The header’s Epic and HLD fields are generated workflow identifiers.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Standalone feature — no parent HLD. Design directly against the repo, grounded on the s1 analyze passes. There are no HLD shared contracts to honour.

boundary.internal: Allow independent turns in concurrent VS Code chats

preconditions: Detached live CLI occupies capacity. A missing CLI identity is unresolved until session-lock and output evidence exclude a live child.
postconditions: Compare original token under transaction before any mutation. Admission and reclaim mint a new unique epoch. Same-window live CLI reclaim follows existing lease grace and liveness rules. Other dead-window recovery finalizes only after both old writer and CLI are verified gone.
Remove standalone release from normal worker callbacks. A matching terminal transaction releases its own lease, and unknown liveness retains the slot.

The process probe used by queue setup and worker returns a tagged observation: present with verified start time, absent with a definitive OS no-process result, or unknown for permission errors, timeout or unreadable identity. A present PID with a known start time different from the recorded start time proves replacement. A present PID with the same start time, a missing recorded start time, or unavailable current start time cannot prove departure. Only definitive absence or verified replacement authorizes old-owner recovery. Unknown evidence retains the lease and defers migration. Recheck the observed lease token in the transaction after probing.

api.name: StreamAdapter
api.signature: resume(req: ResumeRequest, opts?: ResumeOptions): AsyncIterable<TurnEvent>; TurnProcess.stopVerified(): Promise<boolean>

parameters.name: req
parameters.purpose: Persisted cursor, PID and recorded process start time for this turn

parameters.name: opts
parameters.purpose: Existing attach, checkpoint, drain and abort hooks

returns.meaning: Resumed output events and a positive Stop result only when process exit is verified.

errors.condition: Output cannot establish completion and process identity is unknown

preconditions: Queue, adapter, foreground follower and detached observer use the same tagged process observation. A missing PID or missing current or recorded start time for a present PID yields unknown identity. A definitive no-process result or a verified PID reuse proves the recorded process departed.
postconditions: Use positive departure proof for the resumed handle’s exit promise and for the tail reader’s finished predicate. Unknown identity keeps the tail eligible to receive real output. Abort or follower teardown releases polling resources without resolving process exit. No synthetic terminal or verified exit follows an unknown observation.

Real provider terminal output completes the matching logical turn after the existing drain contract. If the tail closes without terminal evidence and process departure is unverified, emit an observationFailure event. A bare segment end or transport error does not prove process exit. Keep the existing cursor, pin, pending decisions, lease, original start time and last progress. Schedule re-observation through existing bounded retry paths.

A resumed handle signals only the positively matched recorded process using the existing guarded signal path. For unknown identity, Stop sends no signal and returns unverified. A missing handle with retained live metadata also returns unverified. Neither a no-op signal, a follower abort, nor an observation failure can fulfill stopVerified. A later positive exit proof or trusted child exit can certify the stop.

Stop stays scoped to the requested session and turn. On unverified Stop, show that exit could not be confirmed, keep the session active with its last known progress and reattach observation. Resume and observer projection treat observationFailure as nonterminal. Queue capacity changes only on a matching verified terminal transition or fenced departure recovery.

dataModelChanges.details: Repository database owns zero to two live leases. Each lease belongs to exactly one session and references exactly one processing message by seq; unique session_id and seq. A unique opaque owner epoch fences stale writes. Window key and PID/start time retain ownership provenance. Detached running CLI retains its slot. Only verified terminal state or verified death allows release or an explicit fenced recovery.
dataModelChanges.schemaDiff: Replace singleton lease id=1 with session_id primary key and unique message seq; add owner epoch and session/sequence index for message eligibility. Bump queue schema from 2 to 3.

dataModelChanges.details: One repository owns many queued rows; each row belongs to exactly one session and originating window. Rows and sequence survive migration. A session owns many messages ordered by seq, with at most one processing row. Retry and resends preserve existing idempotency and retain the originating session.

Each session may own one current turn progress snapshot: turn ID, turn epoch, start timestamp, phase (starting, working, waiting approval or choice), optional latest safe status label. Persist transitions with the owning live-turn checkpoint, coalesce repeated identical updates, and do not append progress to transcript. Clear only on verified terminal or Stop completion for the same turn. Idle is derived when no active turn exists. Legacy missing snapshot derives a running or waiting state from verified live metadata and pending requests; omit elapsed time when the start timestamp is unknown.

Each session owns one runtime containing its current queued run, lifecycle, approval/choice state, diff scope and progress. Reuse existing runtime contracts; reclaim only when no live turn, pending request, or follow remains. A selected-view generation gates projection and never owns execution. In queue-disabled test seams maintain existing single-session behavior.

errorCases.scenario: Queue ownership changes during a callback
errorCases.detection: Atomic update matches no row for the expected session, sequence and owner epoch.
errorCases.response: Drop the stale callback and stop the obsolete observer. Preserve the replacement lease and its progress.
errorCases.userImpact: A reloaded window resumes its own session without duplicating work.

errorCases.detection: Existing SQLite busy error or failed schema transaction.
errorCases.response: Retry contention through existing queue backoff. Roll back upgrade atomically and report invalid rows without dropping messages.
errorCases.userImpact: Messages remain recoverable and the store can reopen after the contention resolves.

errorCases.scenario: Old client still attached during migration
errorCases.detection: A current or legacy extension host has a live presence or queue lease owner. An unconfirmed identity is treated as live.
errorCases.response: Defer migration until old windows are closed or reloaded and their queue owners are positively gone. A still-live detached CLI is adopted as an occupied slot, only after its old writer is gone.
errorCases.userImpact: The upgrade waits for a safe cutover and retains queued and detached work.

errorCases.scenario: Progress observer loses output while CLI is live
errorCases.detection: Existing lifecycle classifies the failure as observation-failed with no verified terminal.
errorCases.response: Retain last known progress and the lease. Reattach using existing cursor recovery.
errorCases.userImpact: The bar continues to show the last known activity during recovery.

errorCases.scenario: Concurrent turns can affect the same worktree path
errorCases.detection: A repository has overlapping active turns or another turn/external edit has invalidated a rollback baseline.
errorCases.response: Scope diff ownership and follow-up to the originating turn. Fail closed for automated reject/revert for any baseline exposed to parallel work unless exclusive path ownership and unchanged after-image are verifiable. Offer manual diff inspection.
errorCases.userImpact: Chats share the working tree. Automatic undo may be unavailable for overlapping edits, so another chat’s changes are preserved.

errorCases.scenario: PID is present but its start time cannot be read
errorCases.detection: Queue setup receives an unknown process observation instead of a verified identity. The existing boolean helper can return false for this case.
errorCases.response: Keep capacity occupied. Use a definitive no-process result or a verified mismatch of recorded and observed start times to form departure proof. Do not convert an unknown observation into a recovery proof.
errorCases.userImpact: The affected chat keeps its queue slot until its process state can be verified.

errorCases.scenario: A resumed live PID’s current start time is unreadable
errorCases.detection: The shared process observation reports unknown while the recorded cursor has no valid terminal event.
errorCases.response: Preserve liveTurn, decoder/cursor checkpoint, output retention, progress and queue ownership. Resume may still consume genuine terminal output. A Stop request without positive process identity returns unverified and resumes observation without sending a signal. Only definitive absence, confirmed PID reuse or a trusted child exit may prove process exit.
errorCases.userImpact: The chat shows its last known progress and an unverified Stop result until the turn genuinely completes or its exit can be confirmed.

testStrategy.testFramework: Node test runner through tsx, existing fake clocks, fake webview DOM, fake providers and real temporary SQLite.

migration.stateBefore: The s1 queue bundle identifies a single repository lease in the version 2 SQLite database. The s1 session bundle identifies optional persisted live-turn metadata, while progress status is transient in the selected webview.
migration.stateAfter: Version 3 queue retains message sequences, retry state, presence and any recoverable live CLI identity. Session heads may carry additive progress snapshots, and two different sessions may run at once.

migrationSteps.action: Close or reload every window using the older extension. Confirm no live legacy database writer before attempting upgrade. Preserve a consistent offline SQLite backup including WAL state using the SQLite backup mechanism.

Within one write transaction validate existing rows, create session leases, translate any singleton lease through its processing message’s session ID and preserve owner/CLI identity, rebuild indexes, then set version 3. Inconsistent ownership aborts transaction.
Open compatible windows. Recover per-session leases with the existing process identity checks. Derive missing progress on first reattach and persist it only when its ownership is established.

migration.backwardCompat: Old windows are closed during cutover. An older extension reopening the database refuses the newer version. A failed upgrade leaves version 2 intact. An offline backup can restore version 2 before new writes. After any version 3 work is accepted, reverting to that backup would discard newer messages, so stop and reconcile that work before downgrade. Session heads tolerate absent progress and keep existing transcript fields.

alternativesConsidered.name: Shared queue with session leases
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Retain repository SQLite coordination and schedule independent session heads.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Replace the singleton lease with one fenced lease per session, cap concurrent leases per repository, and bind progress to each session and turn in the host.
pros: Preserves one atomic coordination boundary across windows and existing queued records.
Supports independent progress while retaining FIFO within each chat.
cons: Requires a transactional schema upgrade and removing singleton host assumptions.

alternativesConsidered.name: Separate queue files per session
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Use the existing one-turn queue independently for each session.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Allocate each session a separate queue database and coordinate a shared admission limit and recovery across files. Keep session progress separate from foreground selection.
pros: The single-chat queue state model remains familiar.
cons: Splits atomic admission across files, complicates migration, discovery and repository-wide bounds.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Introduces additional state stores and coordination for the same user-visible result.
